$comment: Which React Native this platform supports, and which Hermes to build for it.
A pinned triple: react-native-linux, React Native, and Hermes are chosen and
tested together, the way react-native-windows pins its own Hermes NuGet
version and one exact React Native in peerDependencies. The alternative --
deriving Hermes from whatever React Native an app happens to have -- was tried
and abandoned: React Native 0.81's Hermes wants a jsi header newer React
Native does not ship and names its build target differently, so following the
app leads three compile errors deep into a version nobody claimed to support.
Hermes is pinned here rather than read from React Native because this platform
builds it from source. Windows, macOS, iOS and Android all consume a prebuilt
Hermes; Meta publishes one for each of them and none for Linux. That single
difference is where every version problem here comes from.
To add a version: add an entry, bootstrap against it, and run both suites.
Untested is not supported -- saying so is the point of this file.

supported.notes: 60/60 unit and 5/5 end-to-end, macOS and CI. What CI pins.

development.notes: React Native main, which calls itself 1000.0.0. Where development happens; the weekly drift job tracks it.

known-unsupported.why: Never built or tested. Expected to work, since they share 0.87's unguarded native module lookup, but expectation is not support.

TurboModuleRegistry gates its fallback behind RN$Bridgeless, so no native module resolves without RN$TurboInterop. 0.81 additionally pins a Hermes whose CMake target this bootstrap cannot drive. See plan/10-first-real-app.md.
